Subject: Data residency and retention Qs – hosted API (DataGuard questionnaire)

Hi Marcus / Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time to help with our security review. I'm attaching our standard security questionnaire (DataGuard_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf) — the sections we need answered fairly quickly are the ones on data residency, retention and deletion for hosted API customers. A few specific asks we have here:

1) Do you offer region pinning for hosted API customers so data and backups never leave a specified jurisdiction? If not, where is request processing and transient storage located by default?
2) What are your default retention periods for: request payloads, generated responses, embeddings, and KV/prefix caches?
3) How do you handle deletion requests (soft-delete/soft-retain periods, tamper-resistant logs, backups)? Typical requirement here: confirm timelines for primary data vs. backups.
4) Is there any cross-region replication of customer data (for HA) for the hosted tier? If so, what controls exist?
5) Are snapshots/backups encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for customers on enterprise plans?

We can also accept a short matrix that maps the items above to timelines/policies. If you can return a short Q&A + the matrix that would be ideal.

Target: privacy & security signoff by Dec 7.

Thanks,
Elaine Nguyen
Senior Security Engineer
DataGuard Systems

Subject: Re: Data residency and retention Qs – hosted API (DataGuard questionnaire)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. Below are concise answers; I also attached a one-page retention matrix and our operations overview for your audit team. If you want, we can follow up with a short call to walk through specifics.

1) Region pinning: For standard hosted API accounts we process requests in the region selected at account creation. For customers requiring jurisdictional guarantees (e.g., data must remain in EU/US), we offer Region Pinning as an opt-in capability (policy + configuration) — this is available for customers on an enterprise plan and can be included in a contract addendum. By default, new accounts are assigned a nearest-region routing policy (US, EU, APAC).

2) Default retention periods (hosted API, default tier):
- Request payloads (ingress): retained temporarily for operational processing; ephemeral logs persisted up to 14 days for debugging and rate-limit correlation, then purged.
- Generated responses (eg text completions): transient by default; persisted only if your account calls the store endpoint or enables retention for analytics. If persisted, default retention 30 days unless a longer TTL is configured.
- Embeddings and vector indexes: we do not automatically persist embeddings for customers unless the customer uses our embeddings store product; when stored, default TTL is 90 days (configurable).
- KV / prefix caches (runtime caches): these are in-memory with optional short-lived persisted snapshots for warm-start; typical TTL 1–7 days depending on workload.

3) Deletion process:
- Deletion request: we perform immediate logical deletion from primary stores (soft-delete) and mark records for purge. Primary data is removed from serving stores within 24–72 hours depending on shard lifecycle.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are retained for disaster recovery; standard backup retention for hosted accounts is 90 days. Backups are purged on a rolling basis; full cryptographic wipe of key material is completed at the 90-day mark.
- Audit trails: deletion requests and operator actions are logged in an immutable audit stream (retained 1 year for hosted API, longer for enterprise retention contracts) and available for export upon request.

4) Cross-region replication: For our standard hosted tier we do not proactively replicate customer data across regions for storage. We may replicate orchestration metadata or ephemeral cache state to a secondary region for failover, but primary customer content is kept in the selected region (or the nearest-region default) unless region pinning / enterprise replication is requested in the contract.

5) Encryption & KMS: All persisted customer data (at-rest) and backups are encrypted. Enterprise customers may request customer-managed keys (CMK) via supported KMS integrations in our Private/Dedicated offering; for hosted API we provide platform-managed keys by default. For enterprise hosted agreements we can discuss envelope encryption with customer keys.

Matrix and docs attached: redwood-data-retention-matrix.csv, redwood-hosted-data-ops-overview.pdf.

If you'd like us to tighten any timelines (e.g., 30-day vs 90-day backup retention) for your compliance needs, we can scope that into an addendum.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-matrix.csv, redwood-hosted-data-ops-overview.pdf

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

• Backups: when you say backups are purged on a rolling basis and cryptographic wipe is completed at 90 days, can you confirm whether backup copies are ever stored outside the pinned region (for customers who opt into region pinning)? Our compliance team needs an explicit statement that region-pinned customers' backups remain within the pinned jurisdiction unless the customer provides written authorization.

• Embeddings: we will be persisting embeddings (vector store) for lookup features. Is the 90-day default TTL enforced automatically or is it just a default that customers can change? Also, are embedding indexes included in your backup snapshots?

• KV cache snapshots: you mentioned short-lived persisted snapshots for warm-starts. Are those ever stored in durable object stores that have different regional placement than the primary account? If so, what are the TTLs and do you log which region they're in?

We'll likely need explicit answers to include verbatim in our vendor risk assessment. If it's easier I can send the exact phrasing you'd prefer.

Thanks,
Elaine

Quick internal add / public clarification:

- For region-pinned customers: backups and snapshots are constrained to the pinned region for hosted accounts where region pinning is explicitly enabled and contracted. We never move backup copies outside of that jurisdiction without written customer consent. I'll flag INF-4122 for a formal KB entry that we can share with DataGuard.

- Embeddings TTL: the 90-day TTL is a configurable policy on the embeddings store. By default it is applied automatically to new stores created via the hosted embeddings product. Customers can request longer or shorter TTLs; changes are audited. Embedding indexes are included in standard snapshot/backup cycles (they are part of persisted stores).

- KV snapshots: persisted snapshots used for warm start are kept in the same region as the account by default. Their persistence is intentionally short (1–7 days) and they are not part of long-term backups unless explicitly configured. Region metadata is logged for each snapshot and visible in the operations audit export.

Marcus — happy to draft the exact vendor-assessment phrasing for Elaine if you want.

—Karthik
Director, Product — Hosting & Operations
Redwood Inference
